sections.html:
Most of the county's tax work happens in the Plato Building at 90 Plato Blvd. West in Saint Paul, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Property Tax Services (651-266-2222) mails statements, takes payments and reviews penalty requests. The County Assessor (651-266-2131) estimates value and class. A separate line, 651-266-2002, covers delinquent tax information.

The same building also houses the Recorder, the Examiner of Titles and the tax-forfeited land office, so a seller who needs a payoff and then a recorded deed can finish most errands under one roof. Bring the parcel number, your ID and the closing date, and ask for the payoff and the current-year installment status together. The county's online Property Tax and Value Lookup lets you check taxes and values by parcel.

sections.h2: Ramsey County housing and the 2026 assessment
sections.html:
Saint Paul is the county seat and largest city, and Ramsey is the state's most densely settled county. Population is 541,623, down 1.9% from the 2020 base. There are 238,541 housing units across 221,327 households, and only 60.6% are owner-occupied. Median owner-occupied value is $326,600, median gross rent is $1,329, and median household income is $81,568.

With nearly four in ten households renting, buyers read the tax statement closely, and a seller should have it ready.

The 2026 Assessor's Report shows total assessed value of real property up by $1.4 billion to $78.12 billion, the highest figure in county history, even after a $66.9 million decline in apartment value. The 2026 values rest on sales that closed during 2025. If your notice showed a bigger jump than your neighbors', the Assessor can explain what drove the change on your parcel. Appraisers walk properties through the year to keep the data consistent, following state requirements for on-site inspections.

Every owner gets two mailings per parcel. In mid-March comes the tax statement showing the first and second half for the year, together with the value notice that sets next year's tax. The second mailing, in November, is the proposed tax notice with the amounts being considered for the following year and the dates of budget meetings. Owners who sign up for eNoticesOnline receive them electronically.

Proposed notices for 2027 are delivered between November 11 and 24. The county's public hearing on its proposed 2027 supplemental budget and levy is Thursday, December 3 at 6 p.m. at the Saint Paul City Hall and Ramsey County Courthouse, 15 W Kellogg Blvd. Comments there are passed to the cities, school districts and other taxing bodies.

sections.h2: How do I dispute my value?
sections.html:
Your first move is a call to the Assessor at 651-266-2131, since many questions end there. Here is what to expect:

  • You will not reach an appraiser right away.
  • Staff will ask what your concern is.
  • An appraiser should call you back within three days.

You can mail or email supporting papers such as a recent appraisal or a purchase record. The appraiser will say which format works best. If the phone review does not settle it, the county's appeals page describes open book meetings and formal petitions. Keep paying the tax while a petition is pending, or it can be dismissed automatically. Board dates print on each value notice, so confirm them with the Assessor.

Homes are billed in two installments. The first half is due May 15 and the second half October 15, and a weekend due date moves to the next business day. If a bill totals $100 or less, all of it is due in the spring. Manufactured homes pay August 31 and November 15. Partial payments are taken, and late payments go to penalty first, then to tax. A returned payment costs $30.

sections.h2: Can the county waive a late penalty?
sections.html:
The county allows one waiver. An owner may request one penalty waiver per parcel every ten years, for either the first or the second half but not both. A first-half request must arrive between May 16 and October 15, and a second-half request between October 16 and December 20. You sign the form and send it with the payment, postmarked or dropped off by the deadline. The county refuses the waiver if the payment bounced, if the parcel has delinquent tax or a payment-plan contract, or if the waiver was used in the last ten years.

Separately, owners can ask the Auditor/Treasurer for an abatement of penalty, interest or costs in cases of exceptional hardship, such as a hospital stay. Call 651-266-2222 to ask. If the county says no, staff will walk through other relief and can set up a partial payment schedule.

Tax turns delinquent on January 1 of the following year. The county then adds interest at 10 percent a year, plus a $25 delinquent fee for publication and notice. Owners have three years to redeem the property before the forfeiture process begins. Notice comes four ways: a courtesy letter in the first week of April, a published list of parcels in a county newspaper for two weeks in May, service of notice by the sheriff, and a certified letter in June.

A Confession of Judgment is the county's formal payment plan. The auditor decides whether it runs five or ten years, a $100 processing fee applies per contract, and interest is 7 percent a year on the unpaid balance. Current tax must be paid on time each year, and an owner can make no more than two such contracts on one parcel. Vacant land is not eligible.

Before listing, call Delinquent Tax Information at 651-266-2002 for the exact payoff. Minnesota Statutes 272.12 bars a recorder from taking most deeds until the auditor confirms no delinquent tax exists on the land. A cash sale moves faster, but it does not skip that check, and the payoff call is still the first thing to do. If the balance sits under a payment plan, ask the county how the remaining contract amount is handled at closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Ramsey County property tax office?
faqs.a: Property Tax Services is in the Plato Building, 90 Plato Blvd. West, Saint Paul, MN 55107. It is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone is 651-266-2222.

faqs.q: Does Ramsey County take partial property tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes. Partial payments are accepted on an installment, with penalty paid off first and then tax. Making them does not stop penalties from growing on the unpaid part, so pay the balance by the due date if you can.

faqs.q: How many years does a Ramsey County owner have to redeem delinquent property?
faqs.a: Three years. Before 2014, homestead, cabin and township property had five years. Notice goes out in April, May and June before forfeiture.

faqs.q: When do Ramsey County's proposed 2027 tax notices arrive?
faqs.a: Between November 11 and 24, 2026. They show the estimated 2027 tax and the meetings where budgets are discussed. The county's own hearing is December 3 at 6 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I ask Ramsey County to forgive a late fee twice?
faqs.a: The standard waiver is once per parcel every ten years. A hardship abatement request is separate and can be made whether or not the waiver was used, but the county grants them mainly for exceptional hardship.
